findings.highlight: The lights finally go out in the noisy tatami-floored room, and silence returns.
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーに何が起こっていたのか、さっきまでとんでもなく賑やかだった座敷の明かりが消えて、静寂が戻ってきた。
findings.governingReading: Whatever had been happening to Saber, the lights in the room that was extraordinarily lively until moments ago go out and silence returns.
findings.explanation: The English omits the opening reference to what Saber may have been subjected to in the women’s room and weakens the immediate contrast from “until just now” and “outrageously lively” to merely noisy.

findings.highlight: It’s not good for my mental health to have girls my age being rowdy in the same house.
findings.evidenceJa: すぐ近く、同じ屋根の下で同年輩の女の子たちが騒いでいた、というのは精神衛生上よろしくない。
findings.governingReading: For Shirou’s peace of mind, it is unhealthy to have girls his own age making noise very nearby under the same roof.
findings.explanation: “In the same house” drops すぐ近く, the immediate physical proximity that drives Shirou’s sexual and social self-consciousness.

findings.highlight: whether Fuji-nee is thinking at all or not.
findings.evidenceJa: そもそも藤ねえは何を考えているのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou wonders, fundamentally, what Taiga is thinking.
findings.explanation: The English changes the object of Taiga’s thought into a joke that she may not think at all, adding a sharper insult absent from the source.

findings.highlight: I quietly make my way to the door so I won’t wake them up.
findings.evidenceJa: 足音を殺して部屋の襖に手をかけた。
findings.governingReading: Silencing his footsteps so the sleeping women will not notice, Shirou puts his hand on his room’s sliding door.
findings.explanation: The English turns a completed, precise stealth action at the fusuma into merely moving toward a generic door and changes avoiding detection into avoiding waking them.

findings.evidenceJa: 切りつける風は冷たい。
findings.governingReading: The wind that cuts against him is cold.
findings.explanation: The English drops the cutting physical action of the wind and leaves only temperature, weakening the hostile winter-night atmosphere.

findings.highlight: The teaching of archery focuses on accuracy, piercing strength, and endurance.
findings.evidenceJa: 弓道における中貫久の教え。
findings.governingReading: This is the kyudo teaching called chū-kan-kyū: hitting, penetration, and sustained continuance.
findings.explanation: The English converts a named three-part doctrine into a generic statement about what archery focuses on, erasing the term that structures Shirou’s analogy for continued magecraft training.

findings.highlight: I think there was something in an archery manual…
findings.evidenceJa: たしか中要秘刊集あたりにあった言葉だ。
findings.governingReading: Shirou recalls that the saying appeared in a work around the Chūyō Hikan-shū.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the specifically remembered title with an indefinite “an archery manual,” weakening Shirou’s textual knowledge and the quotation’s provenance.

findings.highlight: I have to repeat it before I forget the sensation.
findings.evidenceJa: その感覚を忘れないうちに繰り返して、確実にモノにしなければ勿体ない。
findings.governingReading: He must repeat the spell before the sensation fades and make the technique securely his own; failing to capitalize on the success would be a waste.
findings.explanation: The English preserves repetition before forgetting but omits the goal of reliable mastery and the evaluative reason that letting the opportunity pass would be wasteful.

findings.highlight: I narrow my eyes and breathe out.
findings.evidenceJa: 目を半眼にして肺の中身を絞り出す。
findings.governingReading: Shirou lets his eyes fall half-lidded and squeezes the contents from his lungs.
findings.explanation: The English changes the meditative half-lidded gaze into narrowed eyes and reduces forceful, complete lung-emptying to ordinary exhalation, weakening the bodily ritual.

findings.highlight: …And how one should shoot more than 200 arrows a day…
findings.evidenceJa: 故に、日に二百以上の矢数をかけよ……とかなんとか。
findings.governingReading: Therefore, it says something like, “shoot at least two hundred arrows a day,” or words to that effect.
findings.explanation: The source's 二百以上 means at least 200, whereas “more than 200” excludes exactly 200. とかなんとか also explicitly marks the wording as approximate and half-remembered, but the English presents the instruction as a clean remembered quotation despite the source's repeated uncertainty markers. This makes Shirou's recollection both numerically stricter and more exact than it is.

findings.highlight: I clear my head from all hesitations, and I engross myself in the familiar training.
findings.evidenceJa: 未熟な迷いを一切忘れるほど思考を無にして、慣れ親しんだ鍛練に没頭した。
findings.governingReading: Shirou empties thought to the point of forgetting every immature hesitation and immerses himself in familiar training.
findings.explanation: The English retains clearing and immersion but removes the degree/result relation: his thought becomes nothing so thoroughly that the immature hesitations are forgotten. It also renders “engross myself” in stiff, Japanese-shaped English.
